title: HoVer: A Dataset for Many-Hop Fact Extraction And Claim Verification
authors: Yichen Jiang; Shikha Bordia; Zheng Zhong; Charles Dognin; Maneesh Singh; Mohit Bansal
task_description: Retrieve distributed evidence across multiple Wikipedia articles and verify claims requiring many hops.
outputs_or_labels: Veracity labels plus multi-sentence gold evidence sets for 2–6 hop chains.
pipeline_gap_filled: Recursive evidence chains; claim-to-source traversal; evidence-set completeness.
artifact_access_status: paper page/PDF verified; dataset download not independently verified
evidence_basis: ACL record identifies HoVer as a many-hop evidence extraction and claim-verification dataset; retained project evidence describes 2–6-hop chains and complementary evidence.
limitations: Wikipedia-only; attribution, source ownership, and disagreement are not central.
why_relevant: Core benchmark for recursive chain traversal and distributed evidence completeness.

title: EX-FEVER: A Dataset for Multi-hop Explainable Fact Verification
authors: Huanhuan Ma; Weizhi Xu; Yifan Wei; Liuji Chen; Liang Wang; Qiang Liu; Shu Wu; Liang Wang
task_description: Verify multi-hop claims while producing explanations that expose reasoning paths.
inputs: More than 60,000 claims synthesized from hyperlinked Wikipedia documents.
outputs_or_labels: Veracity labels and explanations outlining reasoning paths; retrieval, explanation, and verification evaluation.
pipeline_gap_filled: Recursive evidence chains; inspectable reasoning paths; claim-to-source traversal.
artifact_access_status: paper page/PDF verified; dataset download not independently verified
evidence_basis: ACL abstract states >60,000 claims, 2/3-hop reasoning, veracity labels, and path explanations.
limitations: Claims are derived or modified from Wikipedia; attribution and conflicting-source modeling are absent.
why_relevant: Best direct candidate for chain-aware explanation evaluation rather than final-verdict-only scoring.

title: The Fact Extraction and VERification Over Unstructured and Structured information (FEVEROUS) Shared Task
authors: Rami Aly; Zhijiang Guo; Michael Sejr Schlichtkrull; James Thorne; Andreas Vlachos; Christos Christodoulopoulos; Oana Cocarascu; Arpit Mittal
task_description: Verify human-authored claims using evidence from Wikipedia text, tables, and lists, returning evidence plus a verdict.
inputs: Human-authored claims and heterogeneous Wikipedia evidence.
outputs_or_labels: Supported/Refuted/NotEnoughInfo labels, partial evidence for NEI, and FEVEROUS score coupling evidence retrieval with label accuracy.
pipeline_gap_filled: Heterogeneous claim-evidence graphs; structured-source traversal; evidence completeness.
evidence_basis: Shared-task paper explicitly requires text and structured evidence, including mixtures, and scores both evidence and verdict.
limitations: Wikipedia-centric; no scholarly-paper provenance, source ownership, or explicit recursive claim dependency annotation.
why_relevant: Strong graph-traversal control where a chain crosses prose, tables, and lists.

title: UnifEE: Unified Evidence Extraction for Fact Verification
authors: Nan Hu; Zirui Wu; Yuxuan Lai; Chen Zhang; Yansong Feng
task_description: Extract and integrate evidence graphs over text sentences and table cells for FEVEROUS verification.
inputs: Claims plus mixed text/table evidence candidates.
outputs_or_labels: Evidence selection and veracity prediction using interactions among evidence candidates.
artifact_access_status: paper page/PDF verified; artifact not independently verified
evidence_basis: ACL abstract explicitly describes a mixed evidence graph and gains on multi-hop or text-plus-table claims.
limitations: Method paper over FEVEROUS rather than a new benchmark; no speaker/source attribution or scholarly provenance.
why_relevant: Useful graph-construction diagnostic for interaction among evidence nodes.

title: Explaining Answers with Entailment Trees
authors: Bhavana Dalvi; Peter Jansen; Oyvind Tafjord; Zhengnan Xie; Hannah Smith; Leighanna Pipatanangkura; Peter Clark
task_description: Generate multistep entailment trees from known facts through intermediate conclusions to a question-answer hypothesis.
inputs: Grade-school science hypotheses, relevant/irrelevant sentences, and a textual knowledge base.
outputs_or_labels: Entailment trees, multistep proof nodes, and increasingly difficult settings from relevant facts to corpus retrieval.
pipeline_gap_filled: Recursive support traversal; bedrock-fact selection; intermediate-claim construction.
evidence_basis: ACL abstract describes the first multistep entailment-tree dataset and tasks for all-relevant, distractor, and corpus settings.
limitations: Textbook science and entailment trees are not source-attributed scholarly argument graphs; support/attack and disagreement are absent.
why_relevant: Best controlled benchmark for recursive support from bedrock facts through intermediate claims.

title: ProofWriter: Generating Implications, Proofs, and Abductive Statements over Natural Language
authors: Oyvind Tafjord; Bhavana Dalvi; Peter Clark
task_description: Evaluate deduction, proof generation, open/closed-world reasoning, and abduction over controlled natural-language theories.
inputs: Rule theories, facts, queries, and proof annotations with controlled depth.
outputs_or_labels: True/False/Unknown labels, explicit proof chains, proof depth, and abductive statements.
pipeline_gap_filled: Bedrock/source dependency tracking; recursive proof traversal; depth-sensitive support.
artifact_access_status: paper page/PDF verified; repository route identified
evidence_basis: Scholarly record identifies generated implications, proofs, and abductive statements with explicit proof structure and depth controls.
limitations: Synthetic rules limit ecological validity; no document spans, source identity, or human scholarly claims.
why_relevant: Excellent structural control for dependency depth and missing/unsupported foundations.

title: Can AI Validate Science? Benchmarking LLMs for Accurate Scientific Claim → Evidence Reasoning
authors: Shashidhar Reddy Javaji; Yupeng Cao; Haohang Li; Yangyang Yu; Nikhil Muralidhar; Zining Zhu
task_description: Jointly evaluate claim extraction, evidence extraction, and claim-evidence link validation in full-length AI research papers.
inputs: AI research papers and over 300 manually annotated claim-evidence pairs.
outputs_or_labels: Claim/evidence span identification, link validation, precision/recall/F1, and sentence-gap diagnostic.
pipeline_gap_filled: Scholarly claim-evidence graph traversal; dispersed evidence linking; bedrock support identification.
evidence_basis: ACL paper states >300 annotated pairs, global reasoning across paper sections, dispersed evidence, logical dependencies, and a released repository.
limitations: Small domain-specific corpus; primarily support links, not recursive cross-paper chains, attack relations, or source authority.
why_relevant: Closest direct benchmark for claim-evidence graph traversal in scholarly text.

title: Fact or Fiction: Verifying Scientific Claims
authors: David Wadden; Kyle Lo; Shanchuan Lin; Madej Karimi; B. C. Wallace; Russell A. Poldrack; Anna Rogers
task_description: Retrieve scientific abstracts containing evidence that supports or refutes an expert-written claim and identify rationales.
inputs: 1.4K expert-written scientific claims and evidence-containing abstracts.
outputs_or_labels: SUPPORTS/REFUTES/NEI-style claim labels and rationale sentences.
pipeline_gap_filled: Claim-to-source traversal; support/refutation evidence; scientific provenance control.
evidence_basis: ACL abstract explicitly defines scientific claim verification, evidence-containing abstracts, labels, and rationales.
limitations: Usually single-document abstract evidence; no recursive intermediate claims or full-paper span graph.
why_relevant: Foundational scientific claim-evidence control and refutation layer.

title: SciFact-Open: Towards Open-domain Scientific Claim Verification
authors: David Wadden; Shanchuan Lin; Kyle Lo; Lucy Lu Wang; Madeleine van Zuylen; Arman Cohan; Iz Beltagy
task_description: Collect and annotate evidence for scientific claims from an open scientific corpus using pooled retrieval candidates.
inputs: Scientific claims and open-domain scientific abstracts.
outputs_or_labels: Evidence sentences, claim labels, and cases where evidence supports only a special case.
pipeline_gap_filled: Open-domain claim-source traversal; evidence sufficiency and partial entailment.
artifact_access_status: paper page/PDF verified; artifact not independently verified
evidence_basis: ACL abstract states pooled evidence collection and analyzes partial/special-case support in open-domain scientific verification.
limitations: Evidence remains mostly abstract-level and non-recursive; no explicit claim dependency graph.
why_relevant: Useful realism extension beyond a closed candidate corpus and exact-match evidence assumptions.

title: AVeriTeC: A Dataset for Real-world Claim Verification with Evidence from the Web
authors: Michael Schlichtkrull; Zhijiang Guo; Andreas Vlachos
task_description: Verify real-world fact-checker claims through question-answer evidence gathering over the open web.
inputs: 4,568 real-world claims and online evidence reviewed by fact-checkers.
outputs_or_labels: Verdict labels, question-answer evidence, textual justifications, and an evaluation requiring adequate evidence plus correct verdict.
pipeline_gap_filled: Open-web source traversal; evidence sufficiency; temporal/source dependency tracking.
artifact_access_status: paper and official dataset page verified
license_status: CC-BY-NC-4.0 reported by shared-task materials; verify before redistribution
evidence_basis: arXiv abstract describes 4,568 claims, multi-round annotations, question-answer evidence, textual justifications, and safeguards against evidence insufficiency and temporal leakage.
limitations: Not explicitly recursive by annotation; web-source provenance is document-level rather than claim-ownership or argument-node level.
why_relevant: Best open-world grounding control for evidence quality and source availability.

title: WiCE: Real-World Entailment for Claims in Wikipedia
authors: Ryo Kamoi; Tanya Goyal; Juan Diego Rodriguez; Greg Durrett
task_description: Evaluate fine-grained entailment between claims and evidence, including claim subparts and minimal evidence.
inputs: Natural Wikipedia claims and evidence pairs.
outputs_or_labels: Claim-level and sub-sentence entailment judgments plus minimal supporting evidence subsets.
pipeline_gap_filled: Claim decomposition; minimal sufficient evidence; bedrock evidence selection.
artifact_access_status: paper page/PDF verified; data link not independently verified
evidence_basis: ACL abstract explicitly reports sub-sentence judgments and minimal evidence subsets.
limitations: No source attribution, recursive hops, or explicit support/attack graph.
why_relevant: Strong diagnostic for whether every subclaim has sufficient evidence.

title: A Benchmark Dataset for Automatic Detection of Claims and Evidence in the Context of Controversial Topics
authors: Ehud Aharoni; Anatoly Polnarov; Tamar Lavee; Daniel Hershcovich; Ran Levy; Ruty Rinott; Dan Gutfreund; Noam Slonim
benchmark_or_resource_name: Claims and Evidence in Controversial Topics
task_description: Detect claims and evidence spans in controversial-topic documents.
outputs_or_labels: Claim/evidence span annotations and detection evaluation.
pipeline_gap_filled: Claim/evidence node extraction before graph traversal; disagreement-sensitive context.
artifact_access_status: paper page/PDF verified; dataset not independently verified
evidence_basis: ACL record identifies a benchmark dataset for automatic detection of claims and evidence.
limitations: Older span-detection task; no recursive chains, graph edges, or source dependency labels.
why_relevant: Low-level segmentation control needed before recursive grounding.

title: SciClaimEval: Cross-modal Claim Verification in Scientific Papers
authors: Xanh Ho; Yun-Ang Wu; Sunisth Kumar; Tian Cheng Xia; Florian Boudin; Andre Greiner-Petter; Akiko Aizawa
task_description: Verify authentic scientific claims against supporting or modified/refuting figures and tables.
inputs: 1,664 annotated samples from 180 papers across ML, NLP, and medicine; figure and table evidence in multiple formats.
outputs_or_labels: Claim verification labels with cross-modal evidence and expert validation.
pipeline_gap_filled: Scientific claim-evidence traversal across text/figure/table modalities; evidence integrity.
artifact_access_status: ACL paper verified; artifact not independently verified
evidence_basis: ACL abstract states authentic claims, refuted cases created by modifying supporting evidence rather than claims, multiple evidence formats, 1,664 samples, and expert validation.
limitations: Cross-modal verification is not recursively linked claim dependency; evidence modifications may not model natural source disagreement.
why_relevant: Important modern extension for graph traversal where evidence is not text-only.

title: HiEviDR-Bench: A Benchmark for Hierarchical Evidence Aggregation in Deep Research
authors: Yubo Sun; Chunyi Peng; Yukun Yan; Zhenghao Liu; Sen Mei; Bangrui Xu; Xuanhe Zhou; Chi Chen; Maosong Sun
task_description: Evaluate hierarchical evidence aggregation from sources to intermediate claims and final conclusions using explicit evidence graphs.
inputs: 2,000 human-validated open-domain and academic-domain questions, text-only and multimodal evidence.
outputs_or_labels: Evidence selection/linking, intermediate-claim aggregation, traceability, citation accuracy, claim verification, and answer correctness with progressive gating.
pipeline_gap_filled: Direct recursive evidence-graph traversal; intermediate claim construction; source dependency tracking.
artifact_access_status: arXiv record verified; artifact access not independently verified
evidence_basis: arXiv abstract explicitly describes explicit evidence graphs, cross-source linking, aggregation to intermediate claims/final conclusions, five traceability dimensions, progressive gating, and 2,000 questions.
limitations: Very recent preprint; artifact, license, annotation details, and benchmark stability require follow-up verification.
why_relevant: Closest located benchmark to the requested end-to-end recursive evidence-chain and claim-evidence graph task.

title: Team Papelo at FEVEROUS: Multi-hop Evidence Pursuit
task_description: Iteratively pursue missing evidence across subsequent hops using next-hop prediction over FEVEROUS pages and elements.
inputs: FEVEROUS claims with candidate pages, sentences, tables, and cells.
outputs_or_labels: Evidence-chain retrieval, next-hop prediction, FEVEROUS score, and label accuracy; pursuit improves through up to seven hops.
pipeline_gap_filled: Operational recursive traversal; next-hop search; incomplete-chain recovery.
artifact_access_status: paper page/PDF verified; no new artifact
evidence_basis: ACL abstract and PDF describe iterative missing-evidence pursuit, next-hop prediction, and gains through seven hops.
limitations: System paper, not a new benchmark; FEVEROUS remains Wikipedia-centric and lacks scholarly claim provenance.
why_relevant: Useful operational stress test for traversal policy and recovery from initially incomplete evidence.

title: SciVer: Evaluating Foundation Models for Multimodal Scientific Claim Verification
authors: Chengye Wang; Yifei Shen; Zexi Kuang; Arman Cohan; Yilun Zhao
task_description: Verify scientific claims in multimodal contexts with expert-annotated supporting evidence across four reasoning subsets.
inputs: 3,000 expert-annotated examples over 1,113 scientific papers, including text, figures, and tables.
outputs_or_labels: Claim-verification labels and expert supporting-evidence annotations; multimodal reasoning diagnostics.
pipeline_gap_filled: Scientific claim-evidence traversal; multimodal evidence sufficiency; source dependency control.
artifact_access_status: paper page/PDF verified; artifact not independently verified
evidence_basis: ACL abstract reports 3,000 examples over 1,113 papers, four reasoning subsets, and expert-annotated supporting evidence.
limitations: Primarily claim-to-evidence rather than recursive claim-to-claim graphs; artifact access and license require follow-up.
why_relevant: Large expert-annotated scientific grounding benchmark for multimodal evidence selection.

title: MEVER: Multi-Modal and Explainable Claim Verification with Graph-based Evidence Retrieval
authors: Delvin Ce Zhang; Suhan Cui; Zhelin Chu; Xianren Zhang; Dongwon Lee
task_description: Retrieve multimodal evidence in a two-layer claim-evidence graph, verify claims, and generate explanations.
inputs: Claims with textual and visual evidence, including scientific chart data.
outputs_or_labels: Evidence retrieval, multimodal claim verification, explanation generation, and graph-based cross-modal links.
pipeline_gap_filled: Claim-evidence graph traversal; cross-modal edge recovery; explainable evidence paths.
artifact_access_status: paper page/PDF verified; artifact not independently verified
evidence_basis: ACL abstract explicitly describes a two-layer multimodal graph, image-to-text/text-to-image reasoning, and a new AI-domain scientific dataset AIChartClaim.
limitations: The paper is primarily a method plus dataset resource; recursive intermediate claims and bedrock dependencies are not explicit.
why_relevant: Direct graph-retrieval diagnostic for multimodal claim/evidence edges.

title: SciCiteVal: A Multi-Domain Dataset for Scientific Citation Verification
authors: Qinyue Liu; Yongxin Zhou; Cyril Labbe
task_description: Verify whether a citation context is correctly supported by an evidence passage from the cited source.
inputs: Over 1,000 annotated citation-context/evidence-passage pairs from full-text cited sources.
outputs_or_labels: Correct, Incorrect, and Unrelated labels; five fine-grained incorrect-citation categories.
pipeline_gap_filled: Cross-document claim-source dependency; citation-edge correctness; bedrock source verification.
artifact_access_status: paper page/PDF verified; artifact not independently verified
license_status: ACL publication access is clear; dataset license not independently verified
evidence_basis: ACL abstract specifies paired citation contexts and full-text evidence passages, fine-grained error taxonomy, and released benchmark resource.
limitations: Citation verification is one edge at a time; it does not annotate recursive multi-hop chains or intermediate claims.
why_relevant: Highly relevant source-dependency control for scholarly claim graphs.

title: MuSciClaims: Multimodal Scientific Claim Verification
authors: Yash Kumar Lal; Manikanta Bandham; Mohammad Saqib Hasan; Apoorva Kashi; Mahnaz Koupaee; Niranjan Balasubramanian
task_description: Verify scientific claims grounded in information-rich figures, with accompanying diagnostic tasks.
inputs: Scientific claims and multimodal figure/chart evidence.
outputs_or_labels: Claim-verification labels and diagnostics for figure-grounded reasoning.
pipeline_gap_filled: Multimodal claim-evidence traversal; evidence interpretation; source-grounded verification.
artifact_access_status: paper page/PDF verified; artifact not independently verified
evidence_basis: ACL record describes a new benchmark and diagnostics specifically for scientific claim verification over multimodal figure evidence.
limitations: Not recursive and less graph-explicit than MEVER or HiEviDR-Bench; artifact details require verification.
why_relevant: Useful complementary multimodal evidence control for scientific source graphs.
